problem: 2-tuples are rewritten to (lo, hi, True, False), silently changing their meaning from closed [lo, hi] to half-open [lo, hi), which changes results of normalize/union/intersection/difference (points dropped, touching intersections lost, difference no longer removes the upper end), makes (lo, None) accepted while (None, hi) still raises, and makes error messages echo a tuple the caller never passed.

Production code imports the reference copy reference_impl and calls its _Algebra.parse unbound with an unrelated self (line 13), adding a runtime dependency that breaks import when intervals.py ships alone and coupling the implementation to its own reference oracle.
The parse docstring stating the return shape and ValueError contract was removed and not replaced with a description of the 2-tuple semantics.
